# Vulnerable symbols govulncheck finds linked into bin/sagegw, which have been
# reviewed and accepted. Anything NOT listed here fails CI.
#
# The gate scans the binary rather than the source tree (see ci.yml for why), so
# "listed here" means the symbol survived the linker, not that SAGE calls it.
# That is the conservative direction, and it is why several entries below are
# chain-side consensus code a gateway never executes: cosmos-sdk arrives whole
# through the shannon-sdk, and the linker keeps what the module registers.
#
# Format: <OSV ID>  # why it is accepted
#
# Review these whenever a dependency moves. An entry that gains a fix upstream
# should be removed from this file and fixed, not left here, and the checker
# prints "stale" for an entry that is no longer reported at all.
#
# Removed on 2026-08-19: three lib/pq findings (GO-2026-6170, -6172, -6173) that
# go1.26.5 reported through an io.Closer interface and go1.26.6 does not. lib/pq
# is still in the module graph — it arrives via shannon-sdk -> poktroll/app ->
# cosmos-sdk/server -> cometbft/node — so they may return; if they do, CI fails
# and someone re-reviews, which is the intended behaviour rather than a
# standing exception nobody rechecks.

# Removed on 2026-08-31: GO-2026-5932 (x/crypto/openpgp), GO-2023-1821 and
# GO-2023-1881 (cosmos-sdk x/crisis), GO-2024-2584 (cosmos-sdk slashing). All
# four stopped being reported by govulncheck v1.7.0 in binary mode after the
# 2026-08-31 dependency bump (x/crypto 0.55.0 among them); CI printed them as
# stale on 40890c9. The cosmos ones are still in the module graph through the
# shannon-sdk, so they may return — if they do, CI fails and someone
# re-reviews, which is the intended behaviour.
